issue_paraphrase: The statistical summary routine raises an unhelpful exception when given a zero-row (empty) DataFrame instead of returning a summary: numeric columns fail with a ValueError thrown from deep inside pandas' apply machinery, and all-categorical frames fail with a KeyError when the code tries to report skewness/kurtosis computed on an empty frame. The routine should instead return a summary frame in which per-column statistics are NaN and the observation and missing-value counts are zero, matching the summary the underlying data library itself produces for the same input.
fix_summary: Short-circuits the mode and Jarque-Bera computations when there are no observations: skips df.apply(_mode) for 0-row input and returns NaN-vectors, and builds a 4-column NaN frame for the Jarque-Bera apply so the skew/kurtosis lookups do not KeyError. Author reference only; must not leak into instruction.md.
notes: Self-contained pure-Python fix in statsmodels/stats/descriptivestats.py; no network needed at test time. Golden test is pytest-parametrized (numeric/categorical/mixed ids), runs in under 1s at 1 CPU. Reproduces on current pandas (3.0.x); pin pandas if the image installs differently. Editable install triggers a ninja rebuild of the Cython extensions on first import (a few minutes); instructing the agent with a plain `pip install .` (non-editable) avoids the reloader entirely.

issue_paraphrase: Fitting the linear mixed-effects model and asking for its tabular result report accepts a documented title argument, but the report ignores whatever title the caller passes and always prints the same default heading. Anyone who labels several reports with custom titles to embed in a document gets the wrong heading silently, with no error or warning, so the parameter appears to work while actually doing nothing.
fix_summary: summary() now only fills in the default title when title is None and passes the caller's title through to add_title(). Author reference only; must not leak into instruction.md.
notes: Reproduction needs no network and no data download: the model is a 10-observation, 2-group toy fit that completes in well under a second at 1 CPU. The fix is a 3-line branch in a 2700-line file; the search space is the summary-rendering code path of the results class.

import numpy as np
np.random.seed(0)
from statsmodels.regression.linear_model import OLS
from statsmodels.tools.tools import add_constant
X = add_constant(np.random.rand(50, 2))
y = np.dot(X, [1, 2, 3]) + np.random.randn(50)
scale = 5.0
res = OLS(y, X).fit(cov_type="fixed scale", cov_kwds={"scale": scale})
np.testing.assert_allclose(res.scale, scale)
np.testing.assert_allclose(res.resid_pearson, res.resid / np.sqrt(scale))
res2 = res.get_robustcov_results(cov_type="fixed scale", scale=scale)
np.testing.assert_allclose(res2.scale, scale)
print("OK")
EOF

issue_paraphrase: When a linear (ordinary or weighted least squares) regression is fitted with a user-specified fixed scale for the covariance, the fitted result does not actually report that scale: reading the scale attribute gives the value the package would have estimated from the residuals (roughly 1 for standardized data) instead of the supplied value, and the "Pearson" residuals — residuals normalized to unit variance — are divided by the square root of that wrong estimate. The result object should expose the scale the user supplied and normalize the residuals with it.
fix_summary: In the fixed-scale branch of get_robustcov_results (used by every fit with cov_type fixed scale/fixed_scale), the fix writes the user-supplied scale into the cached result attribute res.scale, so the scale property no longer recomputes ssr/df_resid and resid_pearson divides by the correct sqrt(scale). One-line change (plus the added regression test covering OLS, WLS and get_robustcov_results). Author reference only; must not leak into instruction.md.
notes: No network needed; reproduction uses only numpy random data (50x2). Golden test test_ols_wls_fixed_scale lives in the large statsmodels/regression/tests/test_regression.py file (import of that module is moderate but runs in ~0.7s for the single test at 1 CPU). The scale attribute is a cache_writable property on RegressionResults, and resid_pearson (also in linear_model.py) divides wresid by sqrt(self.scale) — the agent must realize the cached scale is stale after a fixed-scale fit. statsmodels/regression/linear_model.py imports patsy; ensure patsy+formulaic are installed.
